baseline-large@116000.note: SCALE TEST snapshot, 77% through (116k/150k) - NOT final, but first-ever baseline-large eval. Wins single-domain BPB decisively over routed-large (1.384 vs 1.872), the gap WIDER than at small scale. Still collapses hard on LAMBADA (982.46) vs routed-large (32.39), a 30x gap even with far more training than routed-large has had so far.

baseline-large@150000.note: SCALE TEST FINAL - 150k/150k, fully trained, matched to routed-large. Wins single-domain BPB decisively (1.354 vs 2.009) - unified vocab keeps compressing better with more capacity. But LAMBADA collapses relative to routed-large: 832.21 vs 24.17, a 34x gap. Scale sharpens both sides of the compression/generalization trade-off rather than resolving it toward one arm.

hybrid@150000.note: Matched to 150k (was 75k). Modest improvement across the board vs 75k: BPB single 2.535->2.494, cross 2.841->2.791, LAMBADA ppl 396->381. Switch acc flat (34.85%->34.35%, noise). More steps helped a little but did not change the ranking.

hybrid@75000.note: GradNorm fixed switch acc (27->35%) but lost cross-domain edge; 75k not matched to 150k. LAMBADA ppl=396.23 - beats baseline/SOTA by a wide margin, between pooled (280.5) and routed3 (3199).

pooled2@150000.note: GradNorm + sparse top-2/16 routing, no confidence head - matched to 150k. Regression vs original pooled on every metric: BPB single 2.409 vs 2.384, cross 2.223 vs 2.135, switch 25.1% vs 27.4%, LAMBADA 312.9 vs 280.5. Cross-domain still beats single-domain (2.223 vs 2.409) - the switching-arm compression effect holds - but the GradNorm+sparse-routing change did not help.

pooled@150000.note: FINAL - plateau confirmed: 68k more steps moved BPB by 0.013. LAMBADA ppl=280.52 - beats unified-BPE baseline/SOTA by a wide margin but well behind routed (47.76) and mot (148.4).

routed-large@150000.note: SCALE TEST FINAL - 150k/150k, fully trained, matched to baseline-large. DECISIVE result: beats baseline-large by ~34x on LAMBADA (24.17 vs 832.21) and by ~5x on exact-match (4.2% vs 0.8%). BPB: baseline-large still compresses better in-domain (1.354 vs 2.009), but routed-large cross-domain BPB (1.203) is now its best number of the whole project - the switching-compression effect strengthens further at scale. This is the real, apples-to-apples answer to the scale-test question: the architectural advantage clearly survives scale.

routed-large@40000.note: SCALE TEST snapshot, 27% through training (40k/150k) - NOT final. Already matches or beats the fully-trained 89M champion (BPB single 2.002 vs 2.075, cross 1.541 vs 1.544, switch 28.8% vs 26%) with 110k steps left. LAMBADA slightly behind (56.8 vs 47.76) but converging. Early positive signal for scale survival.

routed-large@52000.note: SCALE TEST snapshot, 35% through training (52k/150k) - NOT final. Now BEATS the fully-trained 89M champion on every metric (BPB single 1.889 vs 2.075, cross 1.419 vs 1.544, LAMBADA 41.3 vs 47.76), and exact-match jumped to 1.6% (vs champions 0.4%) - first arm all session to climb meaningfully off the near-zero floor. 98k steps still remain. Strong positive trajectory for scale survival, still pending the real comparison vs baseline-large.

routed-large@63000.note: SCALE TEST snapshot, 42% through (63k/150k) - NOT final. First real head-to-head vs baseline-large (@116k, 77% done): baseline-large wins single-domain BPB decisively (1.384 vs 1.872 - a WIDER gap than at small scale, 26% vs 3.5%), but routed-large wins LAMBADA by 30x (32.39 vs 982.46) despite baseline having much more training. Scale appears to sharpen the compression/generalization trade-off in both directions, not resolve it in routed favor outright.

routed10-large@20000.note: SNAPSHOT, 20k/50k (40%) into the warm-started cooldown from routed7. nlp branch reinitialized at warm-start, same as routed9 - recovering, but already tracking well ahead of routed9 at a comparable fraction of its (shorter) target: LAMBADA ppl 59.6 vs routed9's 155.4, cross-domain BPB 1.252 vs routed9's 1.532. Consistent with warm-starting from routed7 (already OpenWebText-adapted) rather than the plain champion, plus a shorter, more front-loaded cooldown. Re-check near 50k for the real comparison point against routed7's own final numbers (ppl 23.92).

routed11@100000.note: Bet 1 (copy gate), 100k/100k continued training from routed8@600k. REGRESSED vs parent: EM 1.40% vs routed8s 6.40%, ppl 25.80 vs 19.13 - despite the diagnostic showing 82.8% of routed8s errors were copy-failures. Mechanism verified correct via unit test (real gradient flow) before launch; regression cause not yet diagnosed - candidates: differential-LR destabilization (fresh copy_q/copy_k/gate at full LR vs 0.3x backbone), or the log(p_mix) loss having different optimization dynamics than plain CE. Needs a training-log check (nlp_copy_gate_mean trend, loss curve) before concluding the mechanism itself is wrong.

routed12@100000.note: Bet 2 (deep experts / per-domain LoRA on top 2 layers), 100k/100k continued training from routed8@600k. Small real improvement: EM 6.60% vs routed8s 6.40%, ppl 18.99 vs 19.13. Diagnostic gave this the ambiguous 17.2% other bucket - modest, unconfirmed-by-theory gain, landed almost identically to routed13.

routed13@100000.note: Bet 3, exploratory (precision/margin head), 100k/100k continued training from routed8@600k. Small real improvement, nearly identical to routed12: EM 6.60% vs routed8s 6.40%, ppl 18.94 vs 19.13 - despite the diagnostic showing ZERO near-miss errors (the exact class this bet targets). routed12 and routed13 landing at essentially the same numbers (18.99 vs 18.94 ppl) suggests the gain may be from continued training itself, not either bets specific mechanism - worth a plain continued-training control (routed8 + 100k more steps, no new module) to isolate.

routed14-large@100000.note: Scaled-up copy gate (Bet 1 architecture at 190.5M), 100k/100k continued training from routed7@150k. REGRESSED sharply: EM 0.40%, ppl 30.12 - worse than routed7s own original checkpoint (4.00% EM, 23.92 ppl). Same direction as routed11 - copy gate regresses at BOTH scales, a consistent (if unwelcome) signal that this is a real property of the mechanism/recipe, not a one-off fluke at base scale.

routed15@100000.note: Round 2, Recipe 1 (control - no new module, flat 0.3x LR on 100% of params), 100k/100k continued training from routed8@600000, identical architecture to routed8 (97 tensors loaded, 0 skipped at warm-start). RESOLVES round 1s open question: EM 6.60% (6.80% filtered), ppl 18.99 - within noise of routed12 (deep-experts, EM 6.60%, ppl 18.99) and routed13 (precision-head, EM 6.60%, ppl 18.94). Confirms the handoff docs prediction exactly: routed12/13s small gains over routed8@600k (6.40%->6.60% EM, 19.13->~19.0 ppl) were NOT from their respective mechanisms (LoRA deep experts, margin-trained precision head) - a plain continuation of training with no new module at all reproduces the same improvement. The real lever in round 1 was just 100k more steps of stable training on the existing architecture, not either bet-specific mechanism. Also matches round 2s pattern: routed17/18 (diet phase 2, EM 9.80%, ppl ~17.1) clear this control baseline by a wide margin, confirming the data-distribution lever is real and substantially larger than continued-training-alone, unlike round 1s two mechanism bets.

routed16@100000.note: Round 2, Recipe 2 (copy-gate v2 - genuinely frozen backbone/vocab head via requires_grad=False, gate bias init -4.0), 100k/100k continued training from routed8@600000. CRITICAL FINDING: every number above is BYTE-IDENTICAL to routed8@600000 (BPB single 2.0922, cross 1.1248, switch_acc 0.2775, all 4 per-domain BPB values, LAMBADA EM 6.40%, ppl 19.13, to every decimal place recorded). Root cause traced and confirmed: stage2_modal.pys evaluate()/evaluate_lambada() always call the copy-gate model with targets=None (the inspection/generation code path), and MoTRoutedCopyGateModel.head_loss falls back entirely to the plain vocab head whenever targets is None (mot_routed_copygate_model.py:65-68) - so the copy_q/copy_k/copy_gate mechanism has NEVER been exercised by the official eval harness for ANY copy-gate arm (routed11, routed14, now routed16). Since routed16s backbone+vocab head are frozen and literally the same tensors as routed8@600000s, the eval pipeline reproduces routed8s numbers exactly, telling us NOTHING about whether the fixed (genuinely-frozen, negative-bias-init) copy mechanism actually helps. This also retroactively explains routed11/14s reported EM collapse: those numbers were always pure-vocab-head measurements too (consistent with diag_copygate.pys separately-measured vocab-only-accuracy of 2/60 and 0/60), not a measurement of the copy-blended distribution's output at all - the copy mechanism itself was never actually being scored by evaluate_lambada() in this whole bet. A real assessment of routed16 requires the same hand-built forward-pass approach as diag_copygate.py (or a harness fix to route targets through to _nlp_copy_gate_losses and read p_mix rather than plain vocab logits) - not built here, flagged as the clear next step before drawing any conclusion about routed16.

routed17@100000.note: Round 2, Recipe 3 (diet phase 2 - nlp upweighted ~70%, no reinit), 100k/100k continued training from routed8@600000. REAL GAIN vs parent: EM 9.80% (11.40% stop-word-filtered) vs routed8s 6.40%, ppl 17.14 vs 19.13 - the largest LAMBADA improvement of any bet so far, round 1 included. Confirms the data-distribution lever (upweighting nlp share of tokens) keeps paying off a third time (after routed9/10s source-matching and volume levers), this time via mixture share alone with no tokenizer reinit. nlp per-domain BPB also dropped sharply (2.514 at routed8@600k -> 1.4047) as expected from far more nlp exposure; code/math/science BPB rose slightly (less exposure) but stayed usable. Cross-domain BPB improved too (1.1191 vs 1.1248), so no cross-domain crossing regression.

routed18@100000.note: Round 2, Recipe 4 (copy-structure mining - diet phase 2 + _is_copy_structured filter on nlp source), 100k/100k continued training from routed8@600000. Real gain vs parent (EM 9.80%/11.60% filtered vs routed8s 6.40%, ppl 17.07 vs 19.13), but nearly IDENTICAL to routed17 (plain diet phase 2, no filter): EM 9.80% both, ppl 17.07 vs 17.14, per-domain BPB within 0.001 of each other. The copy-structure filter (admit only nlp docs where a content word recurs with gap>=15) added no measurable gain beyond diet-phase-2s nlp upweighting alone - suggests the gain in both is coming from the volume/share of nlp tokens, not from selecting LAMBADA-shaped documents specifically. Matches the round-1 finding that routed12/13 landed suspiciously close together too; worth a real ablation (same nlp% without the filter vs with) before concluding the filter mechanism does anything.

routed2@150000.note: GradNorm loss ONLY (isolates the loss fix, no other changes) - matched to 150k. Severe regression vs routed champion: BPB single 3.387 vs 2.075 (+63%), cross 2.823 vs 1.544 (+83%), LAMBADA 1598 vs 47.76 (33x worse). Switch acc improved (33.5% vs 26%). Third GradNorm variant (with routed3, pooled2) showing the same trade: switch-prediction gains at a severe cost to language modeling quality. This isolates the loss-function change alone as the culprit, not data density or routing sparsity.

routed3@150000.note: GradNorm + 2.4x denser cross-domain data. Switch acc improved (35% vs routed champion 26%) but BPB nearly doubled and LAMBADA collapsed (3199 vs 48) - the denser data variant badly hurt LM quality despite the switch-prediction gain.

routed4@10000.note: First snapshot, only 6.9% through training (10k/150k) - too early to read into. Decoupled switch head + learned Kendall switch-weight + 2x context, standard CE loss (no GradNorm). LAMBADA ppl=310.53.

routed4@150000.note: FINAL - 150k/150k. Combined fix (decoupled switch head + learned Kendall weight + 2x context) underperforms the plain champion (LAMBADA 234.92 vs 47.76, ~5x worse). Root cause visible in the data: switch-prediction accuracy is EXACTLY 0.0000 (0/4925) - the gradient-decoupled switch head completely failed to learn switching at all, since it only ever sees content-shaped backbone representations as a frozen feature extractor with no gradient of its own reaching the backbone. Consequence: cross-domain BPB (1.992) barely improves over single-domain (2.046), losing the switching-compression effect entirely. The decoupling protected content quality (BPB single is reasonable, close to routed-large) but was too aggressive - it eliminated the switching mechanism's function, not just its interference with content.

routed7-large@125000.note: SNAPSHOT, 83% through (125k/150k) - NOT final, still training. Corpus-matching hypothesis validated directly: nlp sourced from OpenWebText (vs FineWeb for routed-large) already MATCHES OR BEATS routed-large final (150k) on every metric - BPB single 1.968 vs 2.009, cross 1.220 vs 1.203 (near-identical, both best-of-project), LAMBADA 23.90 vs 24.17 - despite 25k fewer steps. Same architecture, same scale, only the nlp corpus differs. This is real evidence the data-source gap (vs GPT-2/WebText) was a genuine, measurable factor, not just theoretical.

routed7-large@150000.note: FINAL, 150k/150k. Confirms the 125k snapshot: essentially plateaued from 23.90->23.92 LAMBADA ppl over the last 25k steps. vs routed-large final (150k, same arch/scale, FineWeb nlp instead of OpenWebText): BPB single 2.004 vs 2.009 (near-identical), BPB cross 1.214 vs 1.203 (routed-large marginally better here), LAMBADA ppl 23.92 vs 24.17 (routed7 better), LAMBADA exact-match 4.00% vs 4.2% (routed-large marginally better). Net: OpenWebText-sourcing nets a small, real perplexity win but is a wash on exact-match and cross-domain BPB - a real but modest effect, not the big lever. Plateauing before 150k is the more decisive finding: motivates testing data volume/mixture-share levers (routed8/9/10) rather than just more steps on this exact recipe.

routed8@198000.note: SNAPSHOT, 198k/600k (33%) into the 4x-data-volume run (nlp OWT-sourced, no warm-start, trained from scratch at champion/base scale). Already close to routed7/routed-large's FINAL 150k numbers despite being a smaller (89M vs 190M) model - LAMBADA ppl 23.84 vs routed7's 23.92, exact-match 3.60% vs 4.00%. Suggests the champion architecture, given enough steps and the right nlp source, closes most of the scale gap on its own.

routed8@575000.note: FINAL-ish, 575k/600k (96%). LAMBADA flatlined vs 496k (ppl 19.25->19.13, EM 6.20%->6.20% exactly) - the volume lever is exhausted at this mixture/recipe. Cross-domain BPB 1.125 is the best in the whole project (prev best routed7 1.214). This is the parent checkpoint for the next phase (copy-gate / deep-experts / precision-head bets).

routed8@600000.note: FINAL, 600k/600k (100% - full target reached). LAMBADA EM ticked up slightly from 575k (6.20%->6.40%), ppl flat (19.13). Cross-domain BPB 1.125, best in the project. This is the final routed8 checkpoint and the parent for all of tonight's routed11-14 continued-training bets.

routed9@24000.note: SNAPSHOT, 24k/150k (16%) into the warm-started cooldown. nlp branch (embedding+head) was reinitialized at warm-start - LAMBADA (155.4 ppl, 0% EM) and nlp-domain BPB (2.00, worse than champion routed's eventual settled numbers) both reflect that recovery, not a failure of the books/upweight approach itself. Backbone + code/math/science warm-started cleanly from the champion checkpoint (their BPB - code 1.59, math 2.56, science 2.05 - already close to champion-scale norms this early, consistent with the 0.1x LR cooldown protecting what was already learned). Re-check once further into the 150k run.

routed@150000.note: CHAMPION - best LAMBADA + cross-domain of any arm; improved from 100k

sota@123000.note: cl100k 100k vocab; worst LAMBADA - vocab is a liability at this scale

sota@150000.note: Matched to 150k (was 123k, undertrained). Confirms it was NOT primarily a training-shortfall artifact: BPB 2.132->2.107, LAMBADA 72149->66681, both barely moved with the extra 27k steps. cl100k 100k vocab is a real, robust liability at this scale, not an incomplete-run artifact.
